EDC mock A

How to use this: Sit this paper two days before the EDC exam, timed (2 hours), with your hard-copy notes and a calculator, and do not look at the marking guide. Then mark it strictly with the guide below. The paper is modelled on the practice test (open book, formula table first, MCQ concepts and then workshop-style calculations). It has been scaled up to a full 2-hour final covering the whole course. About 43% of the marks are on diodes and BJTs and about 57% on FETs, multistage amplifiers, op-amps and power amplifiers. Every circuit is described in words, so you do not need a figure. Draw each circuit yourself before you start the question. That takes about a minute and it earns the “redraw” marks.

Instructions to candidates

  • This is an open-book examination. No internet access.
  • Duration: 2 hours. There are 10 questions. Answer all of them. Total: 82 marks.
  • The numbers in square brackets are the marks for each part.
  • Show detailed calculations: write the formula in symbols, then substitute, then give the answer with units.
  • Unless a question says otherwise: Si BJTs have V and V, mV at room temperature, and all coupling and bypass capacitors are short circuits at signal frequency and open circuits at DC.
  • A sensible pace is about 1.4 minutes per mark. Keep 5 minutes at the end for checking.

Question 1 [10 marks]

Circle the correct answer in each multiple-choice question (I to X). [1 mark each]

I. When the reverse bias across a pn junction is increased, the depletion region:

    1. widens, and the junction capacitance decreases
    1. narrows, and the junction capacitance increases
    1. widens, and the junction capacitance increases
    1. does not change, because no current flows in reverse bias

II. A bridge rectifier with a capacitor filter feeds a fixed load. If the filter capacitance is doubled, the peak-to-peak ripple voltage:

    1. doubles
    1. roughly halves
    1. falls to zero
    1. does not change, because ripple depends only on frequency

III. In a Zener shunt regulator with a fixed series resistor , the Zener is most likely to drop out of regulation when:

    1. the supply voltage is at its maximum and the load current is zero
    1. the supply voltage is at its maximum and the load current is at its maximum
    1. the supply voltage is at its minimum and the load current is at its maximum
    1. the load is disconnected

IV. An NPN BJT is measured with V and V. The transistor is in:

    1. the active region
    1. cut-off
    1. saturation
    1. the reverse-active region

V. A bypass capacitor is connected across in a voltage-divider CE amplifier. Compared with the unbypassed amplifier:

    1. the Q-point moves and the gain falls
    1. the Q-point is unchanged and rises from about to about
    1. the Q-point is unchanged and the input impedance rises
    1. the Q-point moves to saturation

VI. An n-channel JFET has . Its drain current is:

    1. approximately zero for any
    1. equal to
    1. equal to
    1. set only by the external drain resistor

VII. Which device can be operated with either a positive or a negative gate-to-source voltage and still conduct?

    1. n-channel JFET
    1. n-channel enhancement-type MOSFET
    1. n-channel depletion-type MOSFET
    1. p-channel enhancement-type MOSFET

VIII. For a JFET, the transconductance is largest when:

    1. V

IX. In an ideal op-amp inverting amplifier with negative feedback, the inverting input terminal:

    1. is at virtually the same voltage as the non-inverting input, which is grounded, and it draws no current
    1. is at the output voltage
    1. carries the full input current into the op-amp
    1. is at the input voltage

X. Crossover distortion in a class B push-pull output stage is caused by:

    1. the output transformer saturating
    1. the transistors’ being unequal
    1. the efficiency exceeding 78.5%
    1. both transistors being off while is below about 0.7 V

Marking guide

Before you open any solution: write your raw mark per question in the table at the end. Award a mark only if your script shows the line that earns it. If your formula and substitution are right but an arithmetic slip gives a wrong number, take the method marks and lose the answer mark. Accept answers within about 2% of the model answer when the difference comes from rounding.

Where the questions come from. Three parts are workshop-style variants (same method, changed numbers), because the course reuses workshop questions: Q2 is WS3 Q3, Q8(a) is WS10 Q2 and Q10(b) is WS10 Q10. Everything else is new. Every number below was computed in Python.

Question 1: MCQ [10 marks]

Model answer
Part Answer Reason
I (a) More reverse bias uncovers more fixed ion charge, so grows. The junction behaves like a capacitor with a wider gap, so falls (this is how a varactor works).
II (b) , so ripple is inversely proportional to . Doubling roughly halves it. It never reaches zero.
III (c) The smallest , with most of it taken by the largest , leaves the least for . If falls below , regulation is lost. Case (a) is the worst case for Zener power, not for dropout.
IV (c) V means the collector-base junction is forward biased as well. Both junctions are forward biased, so the BJT is saturated. Check: V .
V (b) A capacitor is open at DC, so the bias is unchanged. At signal frequency it shorts , so goes from to . falls (from to ), so (c) is wrong.
VI (a) At , Shockley gives . The channel is pinched off.
VII (c) A D-MOSFET has a built-in channel. It works in depletion mode () and in enhancement mode (). A JFET must keep , and an E-MOSFET needs .
VIII (b) is a straight line falling from at to zero at . At , .
IX (a) Virtual ground: high open-loop gain forces , and the ideal input draws no current.
X (d) Each transistor needs about 0.7 V of before it conducts. Near zero crossing neither one conducts. The fix is to bias both slightly on with diodes (class AB).

Marks: 1 per correct letter, no part marks.

Common mistakes: III: picking (a) because it is the worst case for . V: thinking the bypass raises . VII: choosing the JFET.

Score interpretation

Write your marks in this table first:

Q1 Q2 Q3 Q4 Q5 Q6 Q7 Q8 Q9 Q10 Total
/10 /8 /13 /9 /8 /7 /8 /7 /5 /7 /82

Also add up your score in two blocks: diodes and BJT (Q1 I–V, Q2, Q3, Q4: 35 marks) and FET, multistage, op-amps and power (Q1 VI–X, Q5–Q10: 47 marks). The weaker block is where your last two days go.

Score What it means What to do in the two days left
66–82 (80%+) Exam-ready. The methods are automatic. Do EX2 (mock B) timed tomorrow. Spend the rest of the time on any question where you lost 2 or more marks. Read the traps lists in E8 and E12 once more. Finish your reference sheet (REFE).
49–65 (60–79%) Pass with a margin. Some method gaps or slips. For each question below 60%, reread its listed pack’s method section (section 2) and redo the question with the guide closed. Then sit EX2. Check that your reference sheet has every formula you looked up today.
33–48 (40–59%) Borderline. You have the ideas but not the full playbooks. Focus on the canonical, high-mark types: Q3 (E5–E7), Q5 (E10–E11) and Q7 (E8). Rework the worked examples in those packs. Then do only Q3, Q5 and Q7 of EX2, timed. Make sure the formula table above is on your printed reference.
Below 33 (under 40%) Not yet safe. Do not try to cover everything. Learn four playbooks well: VDB DC to AC (E5, E7), JFET self-bias with the root choice (E10), the cascade loaded-gain rule (E8), and class B power (E13). Each one is worth 7–13 marks. Redo this paper’s Q3, Q5, Q7 and Q10 the next day without notes on the method.

Patterns worth checking whatever your total:
